name: build-agent
objectives: Build the requested Commander agent, optionally publishing and releasing source in this operation. Read checkout-template and build-agent schemas and readiness. Before checkout, define requested action names, descriptions, input/output object schemas and required secret names.

Assign checkout-template with {}. Review its result, then resolve its continuation with build-agent using the returned workspace_id and original instructions and actions unchanged. Keep checkout and build on the same builder under same-agent; never invent a workspace ID. Use the local secret form or Admin Secrets for OPENAI_API_KEY; never put secret values in chat, questions or inputs. Review the saved build result and source.tar.gz artifact.

Recommend sharing reviewed source, but publish only on operator agreement; a supplied repository requests publication. Otherwise ask a linked Publish or Skip question unless already declined. Await actual answers with the operation open; expiry never grants approval. Skipping completes with workspace_id and a concise summary after resolving the build continuation without follow-up actions.

For publication, read publish-agent's schema and obtain owner/repository. Preserve explicit visibility or the advertised default; without either, ask Public (recommended) or Private. Resolve the build continuation with publish-agent using the exact saved source_artifact_id, full source_file descriptor, repository and visibility. Any builder sharing artifact storage can publish without the workspace. GITHUB_TOKEN uses the managed-secret form only for publication/release; missing it must not block a source-only build. Preserve existing visibility, never force-push, and inspect uncertain publication before retrying. Save the publication result in the optional report.

Offer optional release after publication; source publication alone is valid completion. A supplied release_version requests release; otherwise ask Release or Finish. Obtain an explicit stable vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version, never invent one. Resolve the publication continuation with release-agent using repository, saved publication commit_sha, built agent_type and chosen version. The default branch must still match the approved commit.

Pending release checks continue automatically with the same workflow_run_id; keep the operation open. Inspect failed or uncertain runs and link the workflow; retry failed jobs in the same GitHub run, never silently dispatch a replacement. Only status released confirms an installable pinned package; review and save that verified release result in the optional report.

Offer installation only after verified release. Honor an explicit installation request or refusal; otherwise ask a linked Install this agent? question with Install and Finish. Failed or uncertain releases never authorize installation. Resolve the release continuation without follow-up actions and complete the build first, including workspace_id, summary and saved publication/release evidence, whether installation is accepted or declined.

If installation is approved, read describe_mission for install-agent and describe_action for spawn-agent. Start a separate install-agent operation with the exact verified package and visibility; assign spawn-agent with that same input through the controller. Never substitute an alias, unversioned URL, @stable or default visibility, or queue provisioning inside the build. Review the saved spawn result, resolve its continuation without follow-up actions, and recheck list_agents and action readiness before completing with agent_id and limitations. Registration alone is insufficient. Inspect uncertain launches before retrying; never silently create another instance. Installation failure preserves the successful build/release.

instructions.description: Implementation guidance for the requested action contracts. Never include secret values.

actions.description: Requested action contracts for the generated agent. Names must be unique. Define them before checkout and pass them unchanged to build-agent; required_secrets are names, never values.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema for an object input, with local references only. Extension keywords are allowed.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema for an object output, with local references only. Extension keywords are allowed.

required_secrets.description: Managed secret names needed by the generated action, not by the builder. Never include values.

repository.description: Optional GitHub owner/repository. Supplying it requests publication after a successful build and source review; otherwise ask whether to publish or skip.

visibility.description: Optional publication visibility. Preserve an explicit choice or the action schema default; otherwise ask Public (recommended) or Private before publishing.

release_version.description: Optional explicit request to release this version after publication. Otherwise ask whether to release or finish with source only; never infer release consent from publication alone.

name: install-agent
objectives: Install 1 to 100 instances of one GitHub agent package; omitted count means one. The spawner resolves an omitted version or @stable separately for each launch and saves that launch's exact version for retries. Use an explicit @vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH pin when every instance must use the same release.

Read spawn-agent's schema and readiness, then assign it with package, visibility and optional count. Omitted count means one direct launch; larger counts propose one single-instance spawn-agent child per instance for controller dispatch. Preserve visibility; omitted means public. For owners outside github.com/defos-ai, each running launch asks an installation question. Answer that saved question: operator first, model allowed after fallback_at. Yes resumes the same execution; No prevents that launch. Do not ask duplicate questions or queue replacement work while it waits. Private repositories use the spawner's GitHub token or managed-secret form; never request token values in chat or action input.

Review every saved launch result and registered agent's action readiness. The batch output describes requested work, not successful installations; its direct child results are collected for one review. Resolve the model continuation with no follow-up actions. Complete with agent_id for one launch or agent_ids for the successfully installed batch members, describing failed or unverified instances in limitations. If none were installed, use an empty agent_ids array and explain why in limitations. Registration does not guarantee every action is ready. Do not invent packages, install host dependencies, request deployment privileges or retry an uncertain launch with a new task. Run work needing the new actions in a separate operation after its preflight is ready.

package.description: GitHub repository URL or github.com/owner/repository[/module/path], optionally followed by @stable or @vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH; omitted version means stable.

visibility.description: Repository visibility supplied by the source list or operator; omitted means public. Pass it unchanged to the spawn action.

count.description: Number of agent instances to install with spawn-agent; omitted means one.
